data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's central premise — that a large service is more resilient because its unified control plane enables 'active-active dynamic traffic evacuation' that decentralized networks cannot coordinate — inverts the actual correlated-failure risk the problem asks about. A globally shared control plane with real-time telemetry is itself a shared cause: a bug, misconfiguration, or compromise there can simultaneously disable the evacuation mechanism and all dependent segments, producing exactly the correlated failure the problem asks evidence to distinguish from merely 'uncorrelated' failures. SRC_001 even names this as a countercondition ('Complexity Paradox') but never explains how the argument survives it. The problem explicitly asks what evidence would distinguish failures that are truly independent from those that merely appear uncorrelated until a shared cause is found; SRC_001 asserts global coordination as a resilience advantage without providing any evidentiary criterion for independence, and its own countercondition reveals the 'independent' redundancy is not independent of the control plane at all. Thus it fails the problem as stated.
